readings.title: Elqanah and His Wives
readings.subtitle: The Barrenness of Hannah
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 1:1] And there was a certain man of Ramathayim Tsophim, of the mountains of Ephrayim, and his name was Elqanah son of Yeroḥam, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Tsuph, an Ephrayimite.
[2] And he had two wives, the name of one was Ḥannah, and the name of the other Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Ḥannah had no children.
[3] Now this man went up from his city year by year to worship and to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Ěli, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, the priests of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, were there.
[4] And when the day came for Elqanah to make a slaughtering, he gave portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters,
[5] but, although he loved <dn>את</dn> Ḥannah, he gave only one portion to Ḥannah, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had shut up her womb.
[6] Moreover, her rival also provoked her greatly, to make her irritable, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had shut up her womb.
[7] And so he did, year by year. Whenever she went up to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, she was provoked, so that she wept and did not eat.
[8] And her husband Elqanah said to her, “Ḥannah, why do you weep? Why do you not eat? And why is your heart sad? Am I not better to you than ten sons?”

readings.title: Hannah's Vow
readings.subtitle: A Prayer for a Son
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 1:9] And Ḥannah rose up after eating and drinking in Shiloh, while Ěli the priest was sitting on the seat by the doorpost of the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[10] And she was bitter in life, and prayed to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and wept greatly.
[11] And she made a vow and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, if <dn>You</dn> would indeed look on the affliction of <dn>Your</dn> female servant and remember me, and not forget <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> female servant, but shall give <dn>Your</dn> female servant a male child, then I shall give him to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> all the days of his life, and let no razor come upon his head.”
[12] And it came to be, as she kept on praying before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that Ěli was watching <dn>את</dn> her mouth.
[13] And Ḥannah spoke in her heart, only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. So Ěli thought she was drunk.
[14] Then Ěli said to her, “How long are you going to be drunk? Put <dn>את</dn> your wine away from you!”
[15] And Ḥannah answered and said, “No, my master, I am a woman pained in spirit. And I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out <dn>את</dn> my being before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[16] “Do not take <dn>את</dn> your female servant for a daughter of Beliya‛al, for it is out of my great concern and provocation that I have spoken until now.”
[17] And Ěli answered and said, “Go in peace, and the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl give you <dn>את</dn> your petition which you have asked of <dn>Him</dn>.”
[18] And she said, “Let your female servant find favour in your eyes.” And the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no more sad.

readings.title: The Dedication of Samuel
readings.subtitle: Lent to YeHoVaH
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 1:19] And they rose up early in the morning and worshipped before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and returned and came to their house at Ramah. And Elqanah knew <dn>את</dn> Ḥannah his wife, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> remembered her.
[20] And it came to be at the turn of days, that Ḥannah conceived and bore a son, and called <dn>את</dn> his name Shemu’ěl, “Because I have asked <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for him.”
[21] And the man Elqanah and all his house went up to slaughter to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>את</dn> the yearly slaughtering and <dn>את</dn> his vow.
[22] But Ḥannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “When the child is weaned, then I shall take him. And he shall appear before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and remain forever there.”
[23] And her husband Elqanah said to her, “Do what is good in your eyes. Remain until you have weaned him. Only let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> establish <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> word.” And the woman remained and nursed <dn>את</dn> her son until she had weaned him.
[24] And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls, and one ěphah of flour, and a skin of wine, and brought him to the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in Shiloh. And the child was young.
[25] And they slew <dn>את</dn> a bull, and brought <dn>את</dn> the child to Ěli.
[26] And she said, “O my master! As your being lives, my master, I am the woman who stood by you here, praying to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[27] “I prayed for this youth, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has granted me <dn>את</dn> what I asked of <dn>Him</dn>.
[28] “So I have also loaned him to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. All the days that he lives he shall be loaned to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” And he worshipped there before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: YeHoVaH Calls Samuel
readings.subtitle: The Word Revealed
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 3:1] And the young Shemu’ěl was serving <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> before Ěli. And the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was rare in those days – no vision breaking forth.
[2] And it came to be in that day, that Ěli was lying down in his place. And his eyes had begun to grow so dim that he was unable to see,
[3] And the lamp of <dn>Elohim</dn> had not gone out in the Hěḵal of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> where the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was, and Shemu’ěl was lying down to sleep.
[4] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> called Shemu’ěl, and he answered, “Here I am!”
[5] He then ran to Ěli and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he said, “I did not call – lie down again.” So he went and lay down.
[6] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> again called, <dq>“Shemu’ěl!”</dq> And Shemu’ěl arose and went to Ěli, and said, “Here I am, for you called me.” But he answered, “My son, I did not call – lie down again.”
[7] Now Shemu’ěl did not yet know <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was not yet revealed to him.
[8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> called Shemu’ěl again the third time, and he arose and went to Ěli, and said, “Here I am, for you did call me.” Then Ěli understood that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had called the youth.
[9] So Ěli said to Shemu’ěl, “Go, lie down. And it shall be, if <dn>He</dn> calls you, say, ‘Speak, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for <dn>Your</dn> servant hears.’ ” And Shemu’ěl went and lay down in his place.
[10] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came and stood and called as at other times, <dq>“Shemu’ěl! Shemu’ěl!”</dq> And Shemu’ěl answered, “Speak, for <dn>Your</dn> servant hears.”
[11] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Shemu’ěl, <dq>“See, <dn>I</dn> am doing a matter in Yisra’ěl at which both ears of everyone who hears it shall tingle.</dq>
[12] <dq>“In that day <dn>I</dn> shall confirm against Ěli <dn>את</dn> all that <dn>I</dn> have spoken concerning his house, from beginning to end.</dq>
[13] <dq>“For <dn>I</dn> have declared to him that <dn>I</dn> am judging <dn>את</dn> his house forever for the crookedness which he knows, because his sons cursed <dn>Elohim</dn>, and he did not rebuke them.</dq>
[14] <dq>“And therefore <dn>I</dn> have sworn to the house of Ěli that the crookedness of the house of Ěli shall never be atoned for, by slaughtering or grain offering.”</dq>

readings.title: Samuel's First Prophecy
readings.subtitle: The Judgment on Eli's House
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 3:15] And Shemu’ěl lay down until morning, and opened <dn>את</dn> the doors of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Shemu’ěl was afraid to report <dn>את</dn> the vision to Ěli.
[16] Then Ěli called <dn>את</dn> Shemu’ěl and said, “Shemu’ěl, my son!” And he answered, “Here I am.”
[17] And he said, “What is the word that <dn>He</dn> spoke to you? Please do not hide it from me. <dn>Elohim</dn> do so to you, and more also, if you hide a word from me of all the words that <dn>He</dn> spoke to you.”
[18] And Shemu’ěl reported to him <dn>את</dn> all the words, and hid none from him. And he said, “It is <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Let <dn>Him</dn> do what is good in <dn>His</dn> eyes.”
[19] And Shemu’ěl grew up, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was with him and did not let any of his words fall to the ground.
[20] And all Yisra’ěl from Dan to Be’ěrsheḇa knew that Shemu’ěl had been established as a prophet of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[21] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continued to appear in Shiloh, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> revealed <dn>Himself</dn> to Shemu’ěl in Shiloh by the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.

readings.title: The Ark is Captured
readings.subtitle: Defeat by the Philistines
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 4:1] Thus the word of Shemu’ěl was to all Yisra’ěl. And Yisra’ěl went out to battle against the Philistines, and encamped beside Eḇen Ha‛ězer, while the Philistines encamped in Aphěq.
[2] And the Philistines put themselves in battle array against Yisra’ěl. And when the battle spread, Yisra’ěl was stricken by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.
[3] And when the people came into the camp, the elders of Yisra’ěl said, “Why has <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> smitten us today before the Philistines? Let us bring the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from Shiloh to us, so that <dn>He</dn> comes into our midst and save us from the hand of our enemies.”
[4] And the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there <dn>את</dn> the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, dwelling between the keruḇim. And the two sons of Ěli, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, were there with the ark of the covenant of <dn>Elohim</dn>.
[5] And when the ark of the covenant of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came into the camp, all Yisra’ěl shouted so loudly that the earth shook.
[6] And when the Philistines heard <dn>את</dn> the noise of the shout, they said, “What is the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews?” And when they knew that the ark of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had come into the camp,
[7] the Philistines were afraid, for they said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has come into the camp!” And they said, “Woe to us! For it has never been like this before.
[8] “Woe to us! Who shall deliver us from the hand of these mighty <dn>Elohim</dn>? These are the <dn>Elohim</dn> who struck <dn>את</dn> the Mitsrites with all the plagues in the wilderness.
[9] “Be strong and be men, you Philistines, that you do not become servants of the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Be men, and fight!”
[10] And the Philistines fought, and Yisra’ěl was smitten, and every man fled to his tent. And the slaughter was very great, and there fell of Yisra’ěl thirty thousand foot soldiers.
[11] And the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was captured, and the two sons of Ěli died, Ḥophni and Pineḥas.

readings.title: The Death of Eli
readings.subtitle: The Esteem Departs
readings.text:
[1 Samuel 4:12] And a man of Binyamin ran from the battle line the same day, and came to Shiloh with his garments torn and dirt on his head.
[13] And he came in and saw Ěli, sitting on a seat by the wayside watching, for his heart trembled for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>. And the man came into the city and reported it, and all the city cried out.
[14] And Ěli heard <dn>את</dn> the noise of the outcry and said, “What is the noise of this uproar?” And the man came hastily and informed Ěli.
[15] Now Ěli was ninety-eight years old and his eyes were so dim that he was unable to see.
[16] And the man said to Ěli, “I am he who came from the battle. And I fled today from the battle line.” And he said, “What was the matter, my son?”
[17] And the messenger answered and said, “Yisra’ěl has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. And your two sons have died, Ḥophni and Pineḥas, and the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> has been captured.”
[18] And it came to be, when he made mention of <dn>את</dn> the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn>, that Ěli fell off the seat backward by the side of the gate. And his neck was broken and he died, for the man was old and heavy. And he ruled <dn>את</dn> Yisra’ěl forty years.
[19] And his daughter-in-law, Pineḥas’ wife, was pregnant, about to bear. And when she heard <dn>את</dn> the news that the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was captured, and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth, because her pains came upon her.
[20] And about the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Do not fear, for you have borne a son.” But she did not answer, nor did she set her heart to it.
[21] And she called the child Iḵaḇoḏ, saying, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ěl!” because the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was taken and because of her father-in-law and her husband.
[22] And she said, “The esteem has departed from Yisra’ěl, for the ark of <dn>Elohim</dn> was taken.”
